meta.title: Ilm — Cross-Tradition Scripture Search
meta.description: Search the Quran, Torah, Talmud, Old and New Testaments together, in Hebrew, Greek, Aramaic and Arabic. Ilm shows source text, citations and evidence — and says when these texts do not address a question.

nav.disclaimer: Scores are weighted judgements from Jev, not generated interpretations.

ranking.byMeaningTitle: Jev re-ranked these results by meaning. One extra request per search.
ranking.literalTitle: Literal term ranking. No model call was made for this search.
ranking.relaxedTitle: Nothing matched that spelling, so results were found by similarity. Check the wording before quoting these.

search.title: Ilm
search.placeholder: Search Hebrew, Greek, Aramaic, Arabic — or ask in English
search.heroTitle: Find what they share — and where they don’t.
search.heroSubtitle: The Quran, Torah, Talmud and both Testaments — in Hebrew, Greek, Aramaic and Arabic, and in translation. When two texts share words, you see which words. When these texts do not address a question, Ilm says so instead of returning the nearest match.
search.noResultsBody: These texts do not appear to address it. Try fewer words, or a different phrasing.
search.partial: These texts address this only in part.
search.unaddressedTitle: These texts do not address this
search.unaddressedBody: The passages below are the closest literal matches, and they do not speak to what you asked. That is an answer rather than a failed search: no passage in the searched texts addresses it.
search.partialTitle: These texts touch on this rather than addressing it
search.partialBody: Every result below is a lead, not a match. Read them as the neighbourhood of your question rather than as an answer to it.
search.verdictDerived: No model was available; this verdict is derived from the ranking, not judged.
search.notJudged: This is not a judgement that the question is meaningless — only that these texts do not treat it.
search.unaddressedBodyNone: Nothing in the searched texts addresses what you asked. That is an answer rather than a failed search — the corpus was searched, and this is not in it.
search.crossLingualHeading: The same theme, in the original languages
search.crossLingualBody: These words were read out of the texts themselves. They are ranked below your own words, so most of these passages are not in the results above — {count} more {count, plural, one {passage} other {passages}} across {texts, plural, one {one text} other {# texts}}.

journey.title: Journey
journey.description: Passages grouped by the theme they share with the verse you started from. Each group is one context, drawn from across the corpora.
journey.sourceScore: How strongly the passage you started from carries this theme.
journey.singleCorpusTitle: Every passage here is from the same corpus. That is one book agreeing with itself, not a connection between traditions.
journey.noThemesBody: This passage carries no scored themes, so there is nothing to group by. Themes are assigned during indexing.
journey.noPassageBody: It groups the other texts that share a theme with the one you started from. Open any passage and its journey is on that page.

recitation.blocked: Your browser blocked playback. Press play again, or allow audio for this site.
recitation.unavailable: This recitation could not be loaded.

topics.title: Topics
topics.description: Twelve subjects, each measured against the corpus. Open one to see which texts actually say something about it.
topics.unknownBody: This topic is not in the curated set.
topics.noPassagesBody: The passages carrying this theme have not been indexed.

marriage.label: Marriage & the spouse
marriage.blurb: The bond itself, and what each text expects of the two people in it.

children.label: Children
children.blurb: Raising children, correcting them, and what is owed to a child with no parent.

family.label: Family & kinship
family.blurb: Parents, siblings, household and servants — the structures every text here starts from.

neighbour.label: Neighbour, stranger, enemy
neighbour.blurb: Duties toward the person nearby, the one you do not know, and the one you dislike.

the_vulnerable.label: The vulnerable
the_vulnerable.blurb: The poor, the widowed, the fatherless, and those whose debt was not their fault.

giving.label: Giving & abundance
giving.blurb: What is given, to whom, and what is said about keeping wealth while doing it.

truth.label: Truth & speech
truth.blurb: False witness, oaths, and the tongue — what these texts think a word is worth.

anger.label: Anger & forgiveness
anger.blurb: What to do with wrath, how long to wait, and what it costs to let it go.

prayer.label: Prayer & worship
prayer.blurb: How to address the divine, and the disciplines that surround the request.

creation.label: Creation & nature
creation.blurb: What was made, and how these texts treat animals, water and harvest.

law.label: Law & covenant
law.blurb: Commandment, covenant and obedience — where the rule comes from and why it binds.

death.label: Death & what follows
death.blurb: Dying, being judged, and what the texts say happens after.

citation.dismiss: Not a reference — search it instead

library.title: Library
library.description: Passages you kept. Each one is the current text from the corpus, not a copy taken when you saved it.
library.noAccount: There is no account here. This library belongs to this browser, identified by an anonymous cookie — so it survives a reload and a closed tab, but not clearing cookies or switching device. Copying a citation is the durable way to keep something.
library.emptyBody: Use the bookmark button on any passage — a search result, a journey member, a citation — and it will appear here.
library.missing: This passage is no longer in the corpus ({key}).
library.copyFailed: The browser refused clipboard access. Select the text above and copy it manually.
library.noInterpretation: No interpretation is included, because none was written. The permalink resolves back to the passage and the scores, so any claim made with it can be checked.

related.title: Related passages
related.explain: Three different kinds of relation, kept apart. A verbatim match is identical words in two texts, which you can check by reading the other verse. A relation is a model’s judgement. A shared theme is a keyword classifier’s tag — every theme in this app is that, and it is the weakest of the three. No direction is claimed anywhere: the corpus has no shared order across traditions, so which passage came first is not something this data can say.

verbatim.heading: Same words ({count})
verbatim.sourceTitle: Found by comparing the texts word for word. Nothing here was a model’s opinion.

relation.heading: Judged related ({count})
relation.sourceTitle: A model judged these related. Treat it as a suggestion, not a finding.

theme.heading: Shares a theme ({count})
theme.sourceTitle: A keyword classifier tagged both passages. It matches words, not meanings.

compare.title: Compare
compare.description: The passages each text holds on this theme, side by side. Nothing is written about what they mean — the comparison is the texts beside each other.
compare.levels: Scores in the corpus take a few discrete values, so the bar moves in steps: this one admits {levels}.
compare.absentSuffix: at this bar — no passage is labelled for the theme strongly enough to show. That is a fact about the classifier, not about the text, and it is not evidence that the tradition is silent on the subject.
compare.noColumnsBody: No passage in any searched corpus scored {floor} or above for this theme. Lower the bar to see weaker matches.

figure.description: Where this figure is named, in which form, and how much of each corpus carries the name. The names differ and the counts are not like for like; both are shown as they are.
figure.basisPrefix: The identification is the corpus’s own:
figure.total: {count} passages across the corpora below name him.
figure.notice: This passage names {name} as {form} — see where each text names him.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: Ilm has no accounts, asks for no email, and sets no advertising or analytics cookies. This page says exactly what leaves your device, because the honest version is short.
privacy.readBody: Saved passages are stored on our server, not in your browser. They are kept against an anonymous cookie identifier that is set on your device the first time you use Ilm — there is no account and no email. Clearing your browser data deletes that cookie, and the passages saved under it become unreachable. Search history and settings stay on your device.
privacy.searchTitle: What is sent to our servers
privacy.searchBody: Every search you run is sent to our server, because the search runs there. The query text, which texts you had filtered to, how many results came back and how long it took are written to a log kept on our server. That log is not shown to you and is not used to build a profile of you. It is kept so we can see which searches fail.
privacy.thirdPartyTitle: What is sent to a third party
privacy.thirdPartyBody: A search query is sent to Jev, an external AI service we use, so the app can work out what kind of question you are asking and re-order results accordingly. The query text is sent. If you would rather it were not, the app still works: Jev is optional, and without it the app falls back to a deterministic method and labels every score as derived rather than model-produced.
privacy.noSell: We do not sell or share your data for advertising. There are no third-party advertising or analytics scripts on this site.
privacy.rights: Write to us and we will delete it. Because there are no accounts, we can only find a log by the query text it contains, so tell us what you searched for and when — the contact page has the address.
privacy.changes: If this policy changes, the date below changes with it.

terms.title: Terms
terms.intro: Two things, kept short because they are the two that matter.
terms.useBody: Ilm is a way to read and compare religious texts. It retrieves passages that match what you searched for and shows you the evidence for each one. It does not write commentary about what the texts mean, and it does not claim which tradition is correct. Where these texts disagree, Ilm shows the disagreement rather than resolving it.
terms.accuracyBody: Ilm is not an authority on religion and should not be used as one. The search ranks passages by how well they match your words and, where a model was available, by a model's judgement of relevance. Every score says which of the two it was. Verbatim matches are exact and you can check them by reading. Theme tags come from a keyword classifier and are the weakest kind of match in the app, and the interface says so wherever they appear.
terms.quoteBody: The original-language texts are not subject to copyright. The English translations are each governed by their own rights, and several in this app are. Quote the language you want to quote and name the translation.
terms.contact: Write to us and we will delete it. Because there are no accounts, we can only find a log by the query text it contains, so tell us what you searched for and when — the contact page has the address.

contact.title: Contact
contact.intro: Three kinds of message, and one address for all of them.
contact.correctionsBody: If Ilm quotes a passage that is not there, gives the wrong reference, or shows a translation that is not the one it says it is, that is a bug and the most important thing you can tell us. Include the passage and what it should say.
contact.privacyBody: Ilm keeps a log of searches. Tell us what you searched for and roughly when, and it will be deleted. There are no accounts, so that text is the only way to find the record — which is also why it is a short, honest limitation rather than a one-click button.
contact.securityBody: Please report it before disclosing it publicly, and say how to reproduce it.
contact.responseBody: Corrections are the ones we can most often fix, and a confirmed wrong reference is usually fixed within days. Search-log deletions are done as soon as we read them. Security reports get a reply either way.
contact.addressNote: Replace this with your real address before shipping, or set NEXT_PUBLIC_CONTACT_EMAIL.

journeys.title: Journeys
journeys.description: Your own paths through the corpora: passages you chose, in the order you put them in. The lines between them are relations this app found in the text.
journeys.reorderFailed: Could not save the new order.
journeys.emptyBody: A journey is a set of passages and the order you put them in. Open any passage and add it to a journey to start one.
journeys.emptyHint: Add a passage to a journey from any passage page.
journeys.missingBody: This passage is no longer in the corpus, so it cannot be opened. It stays in your journey because it was part of what you were reading.
journeys.noEdges: No relations have been found between these passages yet. That is a fact about what has been searched, not a claim that they are unrelated — add more passages and it may change.
journeys.suggestedHeading: Between passages you have not included
journeys.suggestedBody: Relations this app found, leading out of your journey to a passage it does not contain yet.
journeys.corporaNote: This journey spans {count} corpora. A relation within one corpus is that book agreeing with itself; across corpora is the more interesting claim.
journeys.noNodes: This journey has no passages yet. Open any passage and add it here.
journeys.manageBody: The order is the part that is yours. Every line on the graph was found by this app; the sequence is your argument.
journeys.noneYet: You have no journeys yet. Name one below to start.

speech.syntheticNote: A synthetic voice from this device — not a recitation.
speech.noRecitation: No human recitation is available for this corpus. The Quran has one; the others do not, so read aloud is what hearing a passage here means.
speech.noVoices: This browser has no speech voice installed, so it cannot read anything aloud.
speech.unsupported: This browser cannot read text aloud.
speech.wrongLanguage: No voice for this language is installed; reading with {language} instead.
speech.nothingToRead: There is no translation to read.
